# Data Warehousing and Business Intelligence

Coursework plus a course project for the Data Warehousing and Business Intelligence module at
Wrocław University of Science and Technology. 73 tracked files (measured 2026-08-05): seven annotated
`.sql` scripts, three SSIS packages (`.dtsx`), three SSAS multidimensional projects (`.dwproj`)
holding four cubes, six assignment PDFs, and one Python reference script. The repo builds **two
independent Kimball stars** — see [[star-schema]].

An earlier version of this line read *"57 tracked files … two SSIS packages, three SSAS
multidimensional projects"*. Two of those three numbers have since changed and the third was wrong
when written: there were two `.dwproj` projects and three cubes, and the sentence counted cubes while
saying projects. Both units are now named, because "three SSAS things" is not a fact.

Lab 5 was present as SQL only, and the SQL was the half that carried no information —
`list_5.sql` is `list_4.sql` with the schema renamed. The packages are where the labs differ:

> lab 4 loads the mart with twelve Execute SQL tasks and no data flow; lab 5 uses ten data flow tasks
> over OLE DB source/destination pairs
> — Data-Warehousing-and-Business-Intelligence, git commit 80971dc, 2026-08-01

Two ways to load the same mart is the point of the pair, and only one was in the repository. Imported
source-only: `.vs/`, `bin/`, `obj/`, `.suo`, `.user` and the compiled `.ispac` were left behind, and
the developer machine name in the connection managers is rewritten to `localhost` as lab 4 already
did — see [[import-finished-work-into-git]] and [[format-preserving-invalid-identifiers]].

## Stack

T-SQL on SQL Server 2019 ([[sql-server]]) · [[ssis]] for flat-file landing · [[ssas]] multidimensional
for the cubes · Visual Studio 17.5 / SSDT · one Python-over-[[sqlite]] reference implementation.

## The two marts

| | Mart A — `mart` schema, AdventureWorks2019 | Mart B — `dw` schema, `twtr_dw` |
|---|---|---|
| Fact | `FACT_SALES`, PK `SalesOrderDetailID` | `FACT_QUOTES`, PK `(TickerKey, DateKey)` |
| Grain | one row per sales order line | one row per ticker per trading day |
| Dims | `DIM_TIME` (role-played twice), `DIM_PRODUCT`, `DIM_CUSTOMER`, `DIM_SALESPERSON` | `DIM_DATE`, `DIM_TICKER` |
| Keys | all natural/source keys | `DIM_TICKER.TickerKey` is `IDENTITY` — the repo's only surrogate |

Both marts state their grain in prose **and** enforce it with the primary key —
[[fact-grain]]. The surrogate/natural contrast between the two is the whole of
[[surrogate-vs-natural-keys]]. `DIM_PRODUCT` collapses the source `Product → Subcategory → Category`
snowflake into one denormalised dimension, the opposite move from [[third-normal-form]].

## ETL

Mart A loads dimensions before the fact, and builds `DIM_TIME` **from the source header table rather
than from the fact** — the header comment writes out the deadlock the alternative causes. That
reasoning is [[etl-load-order]]. The load ends with a row-count roll-call and two anti-join
referential-integrity checks: [[verify-the-load-dont-declare-it]].

Mart B lands a CSV through an [[ssis]] flat-file→OLE DB data flow into a `staging.quotes` table
carrying two `CHECK` constraints at the door, then loads the star, then backfills
[[relative-strength-index]] with a four-CTE `UPDATE ... FROM` built on
[[window-function-frames]]. `project/twtr/rsi_reference.py` re-expresses the same indicator in
Python over [[sqlite]] — {{reference-implementation-as-specification}}.

## Findings

- **The rejected design is still shipped.** `docs/star-schema.md` argues at length that an indicator
  must be a measure, not a dimension — and `project/twtr/ssas/Dim RSI.dim` implements RSI *as a
  dimension*, with `RSIKey`, `IsOverbought`, `IsOversold`. The SQL side ships the winner; the SSAS
  side ships the loser. See [[rsi-as-measure-not-dimension]], [[measure-vs-dimension]] and
  [[keep-the-superseded-version-in-tree]].
- **There is no slowly-changing-dimension handling anywhere.** No `EffectiveFrom`/`EffectiveTo`, no
  `IsCurrent`, no Type-2 rows. Every load is truncate-and-rebuild, with `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` at the
  top of the DDL. `DIM_TICKER.ListedOn`/`DelistedOn` is the closest thing present and is a single
  hard-coded row. Stated as an absence, not implied as a feature.
- **Nothing here was executed and committed.** Every row count and RI check is a query needing a live
  SQL Server with AdventureWorks2019 and AdventureWorksDW2019 attached. No output, log, or
  expected-count file is in the tree; "0 orphans" is a query, not a recorded result. Only
  `rsi_reference.py` runs standalone. No test suite, no CI, no Makefile.
- **Documentation drift, four instances.** The two TWTR data source views bind `FactTwitterData`,
  `DimDate`, `FactRSI` and `DimRSI` — **none created by any committed DDL**, which builds
  `dw.FACT_QUOTES`/`DIM_DATE`/`DIM_TICKER`. The SSIS `list_four` schema disagrees with `mart` on
  column set and defaults. `olap/ssas/DIM TIME.dim` exposes only DateKey/Day/Month/Year while the DDL
  defines Quarter, MonthName and IsWeekend too. See [[documentation-drift]].
- **The as-submitted coursework is kept beside the corrected version.** `docs/lab-1-notes.txt` and
  `lab-2-notes.txt` hold the original SQL, bugs included; `sql/01_analytics/` rewrites each query with
  a comment naming what was wrong — [[keep-the-superseded-version-in-tree]].
- Numbering marks **run order**, not chapters: `sql/01_analytics/`, `sql/02_star_schema/`,
  `01_create…`/`02_load…`, `01_staging`/`02_star_schema`/`03_technical_indicators`. See
  [[numbered-stages-in-directory-names]].
- Every modelling choice states its cost in comments — "a day's RSI takes two joins", Wilder's
  exponential smoothing named as the variant *not* implemented, the cubes flagged as "Visual Studio
  project files rather than deployed databases". [[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]].
- The first 7 commits, all on 2026-07-25 inside a **four-second span**, ordered as a curated build-up
  with the README, LICENSE and assets last. [[import-finished-work-into-git]] ·
  [[presentation-polish-tail-commits]] · [[readme-as-guided-tour]]. Per the interview these bursts
  were "just cleaning up local folders" — consolidation, not a release. The 8th, on 2026-08-01, is
  the only one that adds material rather than arranging it.
- No `.gitattributes` and no Git LFS: two PNGs, six PDFs and the SSAS `.dim`/`.cube`/`.partitions`
  files are committed as plain unmanaged blobs.
